physicalNotes: Radius 0.958 Jupiter radii from Barber et al. 2024 (2024Natur.635..574B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Natur.635..574B/abstract): 68,489.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.254 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Barber et al. 2024 (2024Natur.635..574B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARBER_ET_AL__2024): P 8.834978 d
sources.shape: Barber et al. 2024 (2024Natur.635..574B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARBER_ET_AL__2024): a/R* 11.42; Barber et al. 2024 (2024Natur.635..574B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARBER_ET_AL__2024): inclination 88.3 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Barber et al. 2024 (2024Natur.635..574B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARBER_ET_AL__2024): transit mid-time 2458821.8251 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 11 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
